# NovaUI Framework: Game UI Component Library A modular, accessible, and responsive UI toolkit for game development, built with React and TypeScript. Designed for rapid prototyping and scalable integration into game engines, with a focus on cross-platform compatibility and developer ergonomics. ## Acknowledgments This project wouldn’t exist without the collective expertise of my collaborators: - **Alex Voss** (UI/UX design) for refining accessibility patterns - **Samira Khoury** (backend integration) for REST/GraphQL API alignment - **The Figma community** for component-driven design principles - **Storybook** for component documentation and testing Inspired by frameworks like Unity’s UI Toolkit and Unreal’s Slate, but tailored for web-first game development. ## Getting Started / Installation Install via npm: ```bash npm install @novaui/framework ``` Or yarn: ```bash yarn add @novaui/framework ``` Run the development server: ```bash npm run dev ``` Build for production: ```bash npm run build ``` Note: This is a hobby project—expect evolving APIs and limited enterprise-grade features. ## Usage / Examples ```tsx import { Button, Tooltip } from '@novaui/framework'; export default function GameMenu() { return (
); } ``` Components are designed for responsive layouts, with built-in support for touch gestures and keyboard navigation. TypeScript types enforce consistent styling across platforms. ## Tech Stack - **React** (with hooks for state management) - **TypeScript** (for type-safe component props) - **Next.js** (for server-side rendering in hybrid games) - **Storybook** (for component documentation) - **Jest + Cypress** (for unit and end-to-end testing) - **GraphQL** (for dynamic UI configuration) - **Redux/Zustand** (for shared state between UI layers) ## License MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ## Badges [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Focus on: - Testing edge cases for accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance) - Expanding component libraries for mobile-first games - Improving TypeScript type inference for custom themes Follow BDD practices—submit feature requests with use cases, not just code. All PRs require unit tests and documentation updates.
